Act') by appellant challenging the order dated 28.03.2025 passed by Court of Ld. JMFC (Mahila Court-02), Shahdara District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi in Case CIS No 2814/2016 titled as HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.12.24 15:35:18 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr.

2 . In gist, it is submitted vide present appeal that the appellant preferred an application/complaint under Section 12 of D. V. Act before Ld. Trial Court wherein respondent herein was arrayed as respondent no.01 beside other respondents.
Summons/notices were issued only to respondent no.01 vide order dated 05.09.2014.
She was awarded interim maintenance vide order dated 31.03.2023.
Evidence was lead by the appellant.
Respondent evidence was also lead by respondent.
After hearing arguments, the application/complaint of the appellant was dismissed by Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order dated 28.03.2025.
This appeal has been filed by appellant on the ground that impugned judgment of Ld.
Trial Court is bad in law and has been passed in haste without Sunita vs Dharampal on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11721706/
1 application of judicial mind.
The Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances presented before it.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that appellate has proved on record through her evidence how respondent and his family-members were cruel towards her and how she tolerated everything for sake for her marriage.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate mental and physical harassment of appellant by respondent and his family-members for want of dowry and qua beatings being given to her for not fulfilling their unlawful demands.
Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that respondent did not spend even single penny for pre and post delivery expenses of children.
Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that respondent has himself admitted to have been gifted household articles like double bed, almirah, dressing table HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH
Dharampal Cr.
Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10 and utensils in wedding.

Ld. Trial Court failed to consider the complaint dated 12.06.2009 of the appellant which was marked as Mark 'D' in evidence wherein it was mentioned that appellant was admitted in Lok Priya Nursing Home, Delhi in serious condition with bleeding which corroborates the deposition of appellant to have been given beatings by respondent side on 06.06.2009.

Ld. Trial Court failed to consider that appellant has given specific date of 06.06.2009 of giving beatings to her and demand of Rs.1,00,000/- made by respondent side for renovation/construction of shared-household.

Ld. Trial Court failed to consider that appellant has disclosed before Ld. Trial Court that due to injuries received upon her head, she got mentally depressed for long time and was treated at IHBAS, therefore, could not file application/complaint earlier.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that appellant was deserted by respondent, she is living with her parents, has no arrangement of alternative accommodation for her & her children and respondent is duty bound to maintain them.
It is prayed vide present appeal that impugned order dated 28.03.2025 be set-aside in the interest of justice and relief may be awarded in favour of appellant.

The appellant has also filed an application under Section 5 of The Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 20 days in filing this appeal wherein in gist it is submitted that appellant was suffering from viral fever, was infected with typhoid and further being suffering from stones in her gall bladder as well as kidney,
she was admitted in Vardhman Nursing Home, Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh on 27.04.2025, was operated and was called again on 12.05.2025 for removal of stitches, therefore,
could not file this appeal within period of limitation, hence, delayDigitally signed by HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.12.24 15:40:41 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr.
Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10 should be condoned.
The appellant has attached photocopy of medical documents of same with the application.

The appellant has also preferred an application for production of additional evidence/documents in the form of treatment papers of appellant qua mental depression at IHBAS, Dilshad Garden, Delhi along- with this appeal.
Appellant has attached her documents of treatment of IHBAS along-with said application.
3. Per contra, it is submitted by respondent side vide written reply that the present appeal is liable to be dismissed with costs.
Appeal is time barred.
The order of Ld. Trial Court is well reasoned and has been passed appreciating evidence available on record.
The appellant could not specify as to when she was given beatings, when Rs.1,00,000/- was demanded from her, when she made complaint to CAW Cell, Ghaziabad etc. etc.
The appellant was also not able to produce any evidence of dowry being demanded and given in marriage.
The appellant mostly resided in her parental home after marriage, used to leave matrimonial home without informing and used to quarrel upon being asked about her whereabouts.

She always used to threaten to falsely implicate respondent and his Sunita vs Dharampal on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11721706/
2 family-members.

Divorce case was settled between them on 03.01.2009, appellant withdrew her case and agreed to reside together, but, thereafter, she left matrimonial home in same month with all gold and silver jewelry.
Appellant gave birth to female child while living separately.
As evident from peeli chitthi available on record, marriage was performed without dowry and gifts.
Appellant is in relationship with her brother-in-law and used to taunt respondent for his dark complexion.
Appellant has only lived for 2-3 months with respondent after marriage and she did not reside with respondent HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH
Date: 2025.12.24 15:40:55 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr.
Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10
despite petition for restitution of conjugal rights being allowed.
Appellant has failed to establish domestic violence which is prerequisite for grant of reliefs under D. V. Act.
The Ld. Trial Court has rightly rejected complaint/application as being vague and ambiguous.
It is prayed vide reply that appeal is liable to be dismissed on all counts.
4. Submissions of both side heard.
Considered.
Trial Court record perused.
5. Application under Section 5 of The Limitation Act, 1963 needs to be taken first.

It is submitted vide said application that impugned order was passed on 28.03.2025, appellant was admitted in Vardhman Nursing Home on 27.04.2025 for operation of stones, therefore, delay of 20 days happened in filing of this appeal.
Appellant has also attached documents of Vardhman Nursing Home with the application.
Considering same and the fact that there is delay of only few days in preferring this appeal which has been sufficiently explained, therefore, delay in filing this appeal is hereby condoned.
6. Now, this Court proceeds to decide the present appeal in view of the grounds of appeal and response filed to same by respondent side.
Appellant examined only herself as CW1 before Ld. Trial Court.

She tendered her affidavit Ex.CW1/A as her examination-in-chief before Ld. Trial Court wherein in gist she has deposed that she was married with respondent according to Hindu Rites and Ceremonies on 15.12.2006.
Out of this wedlock, male child Shiv was born on 11.01.2008 and female child Shiya was born on 14.10.2009.
Her parents spent around Rs.3,00,000/- on her marriage and gave all household articles, cash, jewelry, clothes etc. to respondents.

Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10
After one month of marriage, all the gold and all the jewellery provided by her parents and their relatives were snatched by respondent and his family.

Respondent side used to quarrel with her on petty issues, did not use to provide her proper diet and on being asked for same, used to be given beatings and taunting for not having brought sufficient dowry.
Mother and sister of respondent used to raise demand of Rs.1,00,000/- from her.
Respondent being habitual drunker, used to misbehave with her, abuse her and beat her under influence of alcohol.

Respondent also used to pressurize her Sunita vs Dharampal on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11721706/
3 to bring Rs.1,00,000/-.

On 11.08.2007, the father of respondent raised demand of Rs.1,00,000/-
and on showing inability to fulfill their demands, she was given severe beatings and was further thrown out from her matrimonial house.
She gave birth to male child on 11.02.2008 and the expenses of same were born by her parents.

On 13.07.2008, she herself went to her matrimonial home with hope of everything must have changed because of birth of male child, however, she was given beatings when she entered her matrimonial home and was asked to bring Rs.1,00,000/-.
On 04.08.2008, the respondent took her and her child to her parental home, left her there and also gave beatings to her along-with threats to her parents to fulfill demand of Rs.1,00,000/-.

On 05.09.2008, she gave written complaint to SSP Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, same was referred to CAW Cell, on receiving notice of same, respondent filed petition under HMA at Karkardooma Courts and matter was compromised on 30.01.2009 between them.

She started living with respondent, but the behavior of respondent side did not change, they again started demanding Rs.1,00,000/-, on 06.06.2009, demand was again raised and on showing inability to fulfill it, she was given Digitally signed by HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH
Date: 2025.12.24 15:41:15 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr.
Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10 beatings
. She called her parents who took her to Lok Priya Nursing Home, Delhi on 10.06.2009 and then respondent side came to her parental home and further threatened them not to lodge any complaint.

On 15.06.2009,
she recovered from injuries and lodged complaint before SSP Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh and FIR under Section 498A IPC etc. was lodged against respondent side.
Maintenance of Rs.1,500/- per month was awarded to her by Principal Judge, Family Courts, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh on 25.08.2010.

sentences.text:
She marked copy of complaint to SSP Ghaziabad dated 05.09.2008 as Mark 'A',
complaint to SSP Ghazibad dated 12.06.2009 as Mark 'B', her medical documents as Mark 'C', copy of settlement deed as Mark 'D' and further exhibited her wedding card as Ex.CW1/1 and her ID-Card as Ex.CW1/2 in her evidence.

In her cross-examination, she deposed that she does not know about expenses incurred upon food in her wedding, about salary of her father, from where streedhan articles were purchased by her parents and what was the value of streedhan articles.

She has however deposed that bed, almirah, sofa-set, fridge, washing machine, sewing machine, CD player,
Cooler and other household articles were given by her parents.
She also admitted in her cross- examination that she stayed in her matrimonial home for only about 2-3 months after her marriage.

She has deposed in her cross-examination that she does not remember if she made police complaint on 11.08.2007, when she has deposed to have been given beatings and further whether she made complaint on 04.08.2008 or not.
She has however stated that she was given beatings on 06.06.2009 and she was admitted at Lok Priya Nursing Home by her parents due to beatings being given on 06.06.2009.
She also deposed in her cross-examination that she HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.12.24 15:41:27 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr. Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10

It has to be observed that onus primarily lied upon appellant to prove her case of domestic violence in terms of Section 3 of D. V. Act with reliable evidence so as to be covered withing meaning of aggrieved person as per Section 2(a) of D. V. Act.
The case of appellant qua domestic violence primarily rests upon her averments of demand of Rs.1,00,000/- from her on account of insufficient dowry and beatings being given to her pursuant to same.
As has been noted above, the appellant could not specify in her cross-examination, the dates on which amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was demanded from her by respondent side.

The appellant has deposed in her examination-in-chief that dowry given by her parents was beyond their means in the form of Sunita vs Dharampal on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11721706/
4 household articles, cash, jewelry etc., however, from her cross-examination, it is clear that only common household articles at best were given by her parents in the marriage and that too for starting matrimonial life.
The case of jewellery articles and cash could not be substantiated by the appellant in her evidence.

Coming to the allegations of beatings, the appellant has deposed before Ld. Trial Court to have been given beatings on 11.08.2007, but no MLC of said beatings could be brought on record by the appellant to substantiate it.

Though, appellant has also deposed before Ld.
Trial Court to have been given beatings on 06.06.2009 for not bringing enough dowry/demand of dowry of Rs.1,00,000/- and has relied upon her MLC Mark 'C' to substantiate the same, but said documents of Lok Priya Nursing Home is related to her examination qua her pregnancy.
No history of any beatings has been recorded in same.
No injury has also been noted to have been inflicted upon person Digitally signed by HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH
Date: 2025.12.24 15:41:35 +0530 Sunita Vs. Dharampal Cr.
Appeal No.68/2025 Page No.10 of 10 of appellant in said document
. In given circumstances, the said medical document Mark 'C' also does not in any way substantiate allegations of beatings on 06.06.2009.

As far as deposition of appellant before Ld. Trial Court qua not being properly/appropriately fed during her stay in matrimonial home is concerned,
it has come in cross-examination of PW1 itself that appellant herself used to cook food in her shared household.
So, it is hard to digest that a person who cooks food in shared- household could be denied proper meals.
So the case of appellant on said aspect is also not reliable.

In totality of circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that Ld. Trial Court has rightly rejected the complaint/application of the appellant qua allegations of mental & physical torture, beatings and harassment for demand of Rs.1,00,000/- being vague and ambiguous in nature.

The appellant has not been able to substantiate her allegations/averments of mental & physical torture, of harassment,
beatings and harassment on account of demand of Rs.1,00,000/- by any cogent and reliable evidence.

The Ld. Trial Court has rightly held that admission of the appellant of having stayed only for 2-3 months at her matrimonial home and further that she used to visit her matrimonial home on and off due to respondent being scuffling with her, raise suspicion as to whether she herself was even willing to stay at her matrimonial home.
In totality of circumstances, the order of Ld. Trial Court is well reasoned and has been passed after correctly evaluating the evidence available before i t .
